summary.headline: Sagility Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.5% YoY in INR to INR 20,321 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin hit 26.3%, and FY27 margin guidance was raised to 25-26%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 20,321 mn ($212.6 mn), up 22.5% YoY in INR and 12.2% in constant currency, with organic growth of 11.9% in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23% to INR 5,353 mn at a 26.3% margin, the highest in six quarters, helped by operating efficiencies, FX tailwinds and geo mix despite higher statutory wage costs. Management acquired Chirok Health LLC (closed October 21, 2026) to build a mid-cycle RCM capability and push provider growth, and raised FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 25-26% from 24-25%. The company now holds a net cash position of INR 1,127 mn, and management expects open enrolment/AEP revenue to be slightly lower than last year.

financial_highlights.change: +22.5% YoY INR; +12.2% YoY constant currency; organic +22.2% INR / +11.9% CC
+23% YoY; margin up from 24% in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR 6,343 mn / INR 5,176 mn; OCF to EBITDA conversion 64.9%, FCF conversion 52.9%

financial_highlights.change: vs net debt of INR 1,962 mn at FY26 end

segments.name: Payers
segments.commentary: Accounted for 89.9% of Q2 FY27 revenue. Management said the mix is shifting toward managed services and AI-led deals, and that a Big Ten health plan win covers over 10 mn members with minimum potential ACV above $10 mn.

segments.name: Providers
segments.commentary: Accounted for 10.1% of Q2 revenue and has grown at about 10-11%, lagging payers. Revenue tapered from some discrete projects with one provider client; Chirok acquisition is intended to accelerate this segment.

segments.name: Chirok Health LLC (acquired)
segments.commentary: Clinical documentation improvement, medical coding, risk adjustment, HEDIS/quality. TTM revenue to Sep 2026 of $13 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin 35.8%, net revenue retention above 115%, 750+ employees mostly in India. Consideration $20 mn upfront plus up to $12.35 mn earn-out tied to CY27-CY28 revenue targets.

segments.name: CareSeed (acquired last quarter)
segments.commentary: Integrated into clinical practice; strengthens Medicare Advantage quality capability and adds mid- and small-sized clients. Contributed to the gap between reported 22.5% and organic 22.2% growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of low double digits in constant currency maintained; Chirok and CareSeed revenue sits on top of organic guidance.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 25-26% from 24-25%; management said it sees 24-26% as the structural range, with possible marginal upside if AI productivity gains are retained.

OE/AEP revenue expected to be slightly lower than last year, roughly 100 bps lower as a share of total revenue (last year about 6%); marginally below flat YoY per CFO; subject to change over coming weeks.
Management intends to repay all outstanding debt in full during FY27.
Interim dividend of INR 0.15 per share approved, payable in Q3 FY27.
No explicit provider revenue-share target given; management declined to give Chirok guidance until late FY27.
capex_capacity: H1 fixed asset additions INR 1,168 mn; H1 acquisition cash outflow INR 1,338 mn.
Employee strength 51,486 at end Q2; quarterly voluntary attrition 25.7%, down from 28.6% in Q1 FY27 and lower than Q2 FY26.
Delivery centre count fell to 28 from 31 in March 2026 (33 in FY25), but management said this reflects counting multiple facilities on one campus as one site; seat count continued to rise.
Some short-term leases used during site consolidation; Jamaica sites closed earlier.
Staffing to capacity for AEP season with some flex capacity available.
105 active client groups; all top 10 client groups above $20 mn TTM revenue for the first time.
demand_pricing: Deal ACV up 18.2% YoY to $40.2 mn in Q2, from wins across 31 existing clients and one new client.
Payment integrity win from a Big Ten health plan is contingency-based, so revenue builds over time.
Clients making more deliberate, senior-level buying decisions for large transformation deals; pipeline skewed to managed services and mid-market Blues plans.
Agentic AI deployments: Synchrony Claims Lifecycle (claims adjudication) and Synchrony RCM Lifecycle (denials and appeals), with humans in the loop.
Management said provider deals have historically been smaller; gross margin difference between payer and provider is about 200-300 bps and deal-specific.
On AI pricing, most productivity gains will be passed to clients, with some retained.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin improvement and what supports the raised guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited operating efficiencies, a small FX tailwind from Q1 to Q2, and favourable geo mix; he expects FX to stay broadly at current levels and efficiencies to continue for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much could open enrolment contribution fall this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said about 100 bps lower than last year's roughly 6% of revenue on current visibility; CFO said it is marginally below flat YoY at this early stage.

qa_highlights.question: Is Chirok a step-up in provider mix, and is there an explicit provider target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is a much larger provider share over time but gave no explicit 2-3 year target; provider share is about 10% today. Investment is mainly the Chirok deal plus a dedicated provider go-to-market team, with no major margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is provider growth lagging, and what is Chirok's growth history?
qa_highlights.answer: Provider growth has been 10-11% with some revenue taper from discrete projects at one client. Chirok revenue dipped in 2023-24 when one client's volumes fell, then recovered; management said the 35.8% margin is broadly on the same basis as Sagility's adjusted EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is there conflict in serving both payers and providers?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said there is no inherent conflict, citing about 15 years of running both businesses and claims-denial friction the company helps resolve.

qa_highlights.question: Will margin stay in 24-26% range or structurally rise with AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said the range remains 24-26%, with possible gradual upside if the company keeps some AI productivity benefits; most gains are expected to flow to clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the minimum wage impacts and delivery centre trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the full minimum wage impact is baked into guidance (Q2 about INR 148 mn vs INR 70 mn in Q1), with Karnataka and Telangana effective end May and 1 June. The drop in site count reflects campus consolidation.

risks_watch: OE/AEP revenue is running slightly below last year, and the number could still shift over the coming weeks.
Chirok revenue per headcount is well below a listed Indian provider peer; management could not explain the gap and will follow up. Chirok pricing is said to be at market.
Chirok's AI disruption exposure in mid-cycle RCM: management says outpatient coding is most vulnerable, while inpatient coding is less exposed.
Provider growth has lagged payers; watch whether Chirok and cross-selling lift provider growth above 10-11%.
Statutory minimum wage increases in Karnataka and Telangana are a continuing cost headwind; any stay would be upside.
Q2 margin benefited from FX and geo mix, so sustainability depends on FX staying near current levels.
Earn-out payments on Chirok (up to $12.35 mn) and the $10 mn+ payment integrity deal depend on revenue milestones, so timing is uncertain.
Possible acquisitions: management said it stays open to clinical capability or client-focused tuck-ins, but named no specific target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and margins, with management raising margin guidance and citing record-level Q2 profitability. More cautious on AEP/OE season, which is described as early and subject to change, and evasive on some detail: Chirok revenue per head, the ACV split between payers and providers, and an explicit provider target were all deferred.
key_quotes: We are pleased with the progress that we have made through the first half of FY '27. The business momentum has been strong.
Operating profitability remains strong with Q2 adjusted EBITDA at INR 5,353 million, or $56 million, representing a year -on-year growth of 23%, with a margin of 26.3%, the highest in six quarters.
But over a period of time, it could marginally increase if we manage to retain the benefits of AI.
Like I said, it's exactly to accelerate the growth in the provider segment.
So this is not an acquisition where we want to try and improve the margins of Chirok.

growth.why: FY27 low double-digit organic constant-currency growth was held and adjusted EBITDA margin guide raised to 25-26%, backed by a Big Ten payer win (contingency-based), 18.2% higher deal ACV and the Chirok acquisition, but no specific capacity or order-book figures were given for the revenue guide.
